topStories.headline: City Puts New Rules on E-Bikes, Scooters and Pocket Bikes
topStories.dek: The Waxahachie City Council approved an ordinance at its November 17 meeting governing electronic bicycles, electric scooters, and pocket bikes throughout the city.
topStories.body:
After months of public complaints and safety discussions, the Waxahachie City Council voted at its Monday, November 17 regular meeting to adopt an ordinance regulating electronic bicycles, electric scooters, and pocket bikes — sometimes called mini motorbikes — within city limits.

Mayor Billie Wallace had flagged the issue publicly earlier this fall, saying she had asked the city manager and Police Chief Joe Wiser to draft a framework similar to those already on the books in several other North Texas cities. The concern driving the effort centered on riders — many of them minors — operating the vehicles on streets and sidewalks without helmets, sometimes carrying multiple passengers, and routinely disregarding traffic signals.

The council first discussed the proposed ordinance at its November 10 work session, then approved the final language at the November 17 meeting. The ordinance covers all three vehicle categories under a single set of rules. Residents with questions about the new requirements can contact Waxahachie City Hall or the police department for details on enforcement and effective dates.

topStories.headline: WISD Weighs Switch to Traditional Bell Schedule at Waxahachie High School
topStories.dek: Waxahachie ISD is considering dropping its current block schedule at the high school in favor of a traditional period-by-period day, potentially starting in the 2027-28 school year.
topStories.body:
Waxahachie ISD administrators brought a significant structural proposal before the school board this month: replacing the high school's existing A/B block schedule — in which students attend four long class periods on alternating days — with a more conventional bell schedule in which all classes meet daily for shorter periods. The change, if approved, would take effect no earlier than the 2027-28 school year.

The idea surfaced publicly on November 13 when reporting from the Waxahachie Daily Light described a board discussion of the proposal. The current block format, reflected in the school's existing schedule of roughly 90-minute class periods, has been in use for some time and is used by many larger Texas high schools. Advocates of a traditional schedule often argue it keeps students engaged with material more frequently and benefits courses that require cumulative practice, such as foreign language and math.

No formal vote has been taken. The WISD Board of Trustees is next scheduled to meet on November 30 at 5 p.m. Residents who want to weigh in can attend that meeting or submit comments through the district website at wisd.org.

topStories.headline: Residents File Petition Seeking Citywide Vote on License Plate Reader Ban
topStories.dek: A petition was submitted to the City of Waxahachie on November 19 asking that voters decide whether to prohibit the use of automated license plate readers within the city.
topStories.body:
Residents opposing the city's use of automated license plate readers submitted a formal petition to the City of Waxahachie on November 19, 2026, seeking to place a ban on the technology before voters.

License plate readers — camera systems that automatically photograph and log the plates of passing vehicles — have been adopted by law enforcement agencies across Texas to track vehicles of interest and assist in investigations. Critics argue the systems amount to mass surveillance of residents who have committed no crime, with data stored in ways that extend well beyond any single case.

The petition filing was reported by the Waxahachie Daily Light on November 19. The city has not yet indicated when or whether the petition will be certified, or what the threshold for placement on a ballot would be. Waxahachie City Council meets on the first and third Monday of each month at 7 p.m. at the Waxahachie Civic Center, 2000 Civic Center Lane.

moreNews.headline: Council Approves Updated YMCA Expansion Plan Adding Putting Green and Bocce Courts
moreNews.body: The Waxahachie City Council approved an amendment to the Waxahachie Family YMCA's planned development at its November 17 meeting. The revision adds a putting green and two bocce ball courts to the outdoor component of the YMCA's larger expansion project, which had already been recommended by the city's Planning and Zoning Commission on November 10. The original expansion envisions significant new indoor and outdoor recreational space at the facility.

moreNews.headline: Kratom Sales Ban Vote Pushed to January
moreNews.body: The Waxahachie City Council's consideration of a proposed ban on kratom sales within the city was postponed at the November 17 meeting; a vote is now expected no earlier than January 2027. The council had been weighing the proposal since at least early November, when it first appeared on the agenda. Kratom is a botanical supplement derived from a Southeast Asian plant; several Texas cities have moved to restrict or ban its retail sale amid concerns about its psychoactive compounds.

moreNews.headline: HILCO Electric Awards Community Grants Through Operation Round Up
moreNews.body: HILCO Electric Cooperative announced on November 19 that it had distributed funds to five organizations in its service area through its Operation Round Up program, which rounds up member electric bills to the nearest dollar and pools the difference for community grants. The specific recipient organizations and award amounts were reported by the Waxahachie Daily Light; HILCO's service territory includes portions of Ellis County.
